paper.title_en: Mid-Circuit Measurement of Optical Qubits in $^{171}$Yb$^{+}$ Ions Using the $^{2}$D$_{3/2}$ Hyperfine Structure
paper.abstract_en: Mid-circuit measurement of individual qubits is a necessary element in the implementation of quantum error correction protocols and allows for the reduction of resource requirements for the execution of a number of quantum algorithms. In this paper, we present a protocol for mid-circuit measurement of qubits implemented at an optical transition $^{2}{{S}_{{1/2}}}(F = 0,{{m}_{F}} = 0){{ \to }^{2}}{{D}_{{3/2}}}(F = 2,{{m}_{F}} = 0)$ in ions $^{171}$Yb$^{+}$. The proposed protocol enables selective measurement of a subset of qubits (target qubits) without destroying the state of the rest (spectator qubits). The method involves the use of an auxiliary state $^{2}{{D}_{{3/2}}}(F = 1)$, as well as a spin echo technique to maintain the coherence of the spectator qubits during the operation. The average reliability of the target qubit measurement operation of 98.2(1)% was experimentally demonstrated, while maintaining the amplitude of Ramsey oscillations on the spectator qubit at least 95.2(6)%. The proposed method does not require the movement of ions or the complication of the addressing system, due to which it can be implemented in a chain of ions of one type and easily integrated into existing quantum processors based on $^{171}$Yb$^{+}$. The capabilities of the developed protocol are demonstrated by an experimental implementation of CNOT gate teleportation.
